tagline: The pivot points of global power
description: Every war has a pivot point: the moment the balance of power moves. Fulcrum Brief explains the wars and crises shaping the world with maps and sourced numbers, and shows what each one costs you.
about: Fulcrum Brief covers the wars and conflicts shaping the world, wherever they flare up, and what they mean for your money and your life. Every claim is checked and every source is named on screen and in the description.
Each video finds the pivot point of a story, the moment the balance shifted, and ends on what it means for everyday life: prices at the pump, groceries, markets, security.
New full videos every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

host.name: Damyan Ivanov
bio: Fulcrum Brief is presented by Damyan Ivanov, based in Eastern Europe on NATO's eastern flank, close to the war in Ukraine and to the shipping lanes and energy routes it keeps hitting.
Each briefing follows the same discipline: find the pivot point, show every source on screen, label claims as claims, and end on what it means for the people watching.

standards.intro: Fulcrum Brief covers wars, conflicts and what they cost people far from the front. Our credibility is the product, so these are the rules every briefing follows.

p: Every fact in a briefing comes from a named source: established news outlets, official statements and data, international bodies and think tanks. The outlet and date are shown on screen, listed in the video description and published with links on each briefing page.
A fact goes in when it is backed by a primary source (an official document, statement or dataset) or by two credible outlets. When only one outlet reports something, we say so.

Governments and armies at war make claims that cannot be checked right away. We attribute them ("Kyiv says", "Moscow claims", "the Pentagon says") and never present them as established fact. Figures that cannot be tied to a date and a source stay out.

sections.h: Quotes and posts, word for word
p: Quotes and social media posts are shown exactly as published, with the real account or outlet and the date. We do not shorten a quote in a way that changes its meaning, and a paraphrase is shown without quote marks.
When a Russian-language source matters to the story, we show the original, read it, give a word-for-word translation, and then check it against the record.

Prices are in US dollars unless stated, oil prices name the benchmark (Brent or WTI), and distances are in miles with kilometres in brackets. Every number carries its date, and snapshots say "as of" with the month.

Our maps are built in house on public map data (Natural Earth), dated, and sourced wherever a line is contested. Footage and photos are public domain or openly licensed (for example US Department of Defense/DVIDS, Wikimedia Commons, Pixabay) and credited in each description.
We do not show casualties, graphic combat or people being harmed.

Fulcrum Brief is independent and not affiliated with any government, party or company. We have no sponsors at the moment; if that changes, sponsorships will be disclosed clearly in the video and the description.
Coverage of markets, savings and prices is news and analysis, never personal investment advice.
We write as analysts, not partisans: we name the actor (Washington, Moscow, Kyiv, Beijing, NATO), give each side's stated position in its own words, and keep our verdicts separate from the facts.

standards.corrections_policy: If we get a fact wrong, we fix it in public. Write to us with the video, the timestamp and what is wrong. A confirmed error is corrected in the video description and on the briefing page, and logged below with the date and what changed. Corrections are never made silently.
